newsitem.title: BULGARIA: IMF mission leader arrives in Sofia for talks.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission leader arrives in Sofia for talks.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) will evaluate Bulgaria's reform performance before deciding on further funding, IMF mission leader Anne McGuirk said after arriving in Sofia on Friday.
"We will discuss with the authorities the progress they made under structural reforms, reform in the banking system," McGuirk told reporters at Sofia airport.
"We will be looking at how closures (of lossmakers) have progressed and at macropolicies, particularly at the budget," said McGuirk.
The IMF twice postponed a $115 million tranche, saying the government must fulfil its pledges to close loss-making state enterprises and speed up privatisation.

In a last dash to convince the Fund of its commitment to reform, the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) on Thursday started bankruptcy proceedings for eight out of nine banks placed in receivership in September.
"It is important for the people to restore their confidence in the remaining banks," said McGuirk.
The BNB also cut the annual interest rate to 180 percent from a previous 240 percent in a move to restore investment in industry and lay the ground for the 1997 budget framework.
By the end of September Bulgaria had already topped annual macroeconomic targets laid out in the 1996 budget which was revised for the first time in July.

Cumulative inflation for the first nine months hit 153 percent against an annual target of 105 percent while the Bulgarian lev fell to 244 to the dollar on Friday against a projected exchange rate of 190.
Two or three state loss-making companies out of the pledged 64 have not yet been closed due to legal problems.

The government, struggling to avoid default on its $10 billion foreign debt, has offered for privatisation some 20 major state industrial enterprises, hoping to raise around $1 billion in the next few months.
